genericProblem: A destructive formal seed can appear available when it either terminates at a bootstrap-only boundary, reuses an L2-only debug channel, writes fixture facts outside their owner command/readback path, or assumes a time-driven terminal state has a user command without explicitly realizing its bounded fixture path.
finiteDenominator: r5-full fixture contract stages, counts and 32 scenario prerequisites
generated edge route registry and seed report pair
DEV fixed clock and fixed OTP issuer activation gates
workspace invitation and password-reset owner OTP issuers
run manifest, credentials, event log and first-failure report boundary
all REAL_COMMANDS_OR_TERMINAL_FIXTURE states and their exact terminal allowlist
the active formal-seed package input and its exact delivery-manifest binding
counterexamples: Root bootstrap SQL is permitted only for the built-in platform identity and its audit/receipt facts.
L2 debug OTP exposure is a separately scoped browser-test transport and cannot establish formal seed capability.
A dry-run, bootstrap-only pass, or report skeleton is not formal seed PASS.
Default runtime profile must have no fixed issuer/clock bean and cannot be converted into formal seed by a header or client payload.

findings.evidence: The formal wrapper refuses with OWNER_COMMAND_EXECUTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED while the existing L2 fixture has an owner-command chain and report helper.
findings.minimumFix: Extract the common owner-command/report mechanics into the formal executor and invoke it only through scripts/dev/seed.

findings.evidence: The fixture contract requires DEV_FIXED_OTP_ISSUER but runtime source only exposes debug OTP when the L2 flag is true; the current DEV manifest records false.
findings.minimumFix: Install a fail-closed, private fixed issuer at owner OTP generation without exposing the value on an edge response.

findings.evidence: The fixture contract requires a fixed r5-full clock, while SystemTimeProvider is the only current application bean.
findings.minimumFix: Do not advance a global clock for terminal data; retain ordinary time and realize only the separately authorized terminal fixture adapter.

findings.evidence: The fixture contract declares inv-expired but the owner HTTP surface intentionally has no expiry command because expiry is time-driven.
findings.minimumFix: Model every terminal state explicitly; for the sole allowlisted inv-expired case create the normal PENDING invitation through owner HTTP first, then use a managed remote, exact-namespace adapter restricted to its state/timestamps/SYSTEM audit/scoped receipt and read it back through the existing invitation API.

findings.evidence: The active CP-U17 package input retained an older delivery-manifest SHA-256 after its declared delivery manifest changed, so the fail-closed static admission stopped before a new managed seed could begin.
findings.minimumFix: Rebind only the active package input to the verified current delivery-manifest SHA-256 and retain the exact hash-equality control; historical non-active package inputs are evidence counterexamples, not a bulk-rewrite target.

preventionDispositions.owningSourceOrControl: phase-retrospective formal seed boundary and fixed-time review checklist
